items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4431

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the division of
veterans' affairs providing information to veterans on how to start a
veteran-owned business


 PURPOSE OF BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to require the division of veterans'
affairs to provide to eligible veterans information regarding
veteran-owned business opportunities.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
The division shall provide a pamphlet explaining how to start a
veteran-owned business in the state.  The division shall also describe
procurement opportunities in the State and include this information
annually in its weekly newsletter.  The information must be posted all
division offices under its jurisdiction, be available at the three
seminars sponsored by the division and be posted on the division's
website. Information shall also be made available at New York State
Small Business Development Centers, the New York state department of
labor One-Stop Career Centers and New York Entrepreneurship Support
Centers.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Veterans in New York State have been and continue to be vital to the
small business enterprises in the State. New York State has done too
little to assist veterans in playing a greater role in the economy by
forming and expanding small business enterprises. Medical advances and
new medical technologies have made it possible for service-disabled
veterans to play a greater role in the formation and expansion of
small business enterprises in New York State. New York State must
provide additional assistance and support to veterans to better inform
them on how to become an owner of small business and how to expand
thereby enabling them to realize the American dream that they fought
and protect.  This bill is one step in the process.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New Legislation.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Minimal cost to the Division of Veterans' Affairs.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law, provided that any rules and regulations necessary for
the implementation of this act on its effective date shall be
promulgated on or before such date.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4431B

TITLE OF BILL:
An act to amend the executive law, in relation to the division of veter-
ans' affairs providing information to veterans on how to start a veter-
an-owned business

PURPOSE:
To require the division of veterans affairs to provide information
regarding resources that are available to assist veterans in establish-
ing and sustaining a small business by maintaining a small business
portal on the division's internet site.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
The division may in consultation with the New York State Small Develop-
ment Center and any other appropriate state agencies when establishing
and sustaining a small business portal on the division of veterans'
affairs website. The division shall include this information in its
newsletter, at the three seminars sponsored sponsored by the division
and be posted on the division's website and the annual report to the
governor and legislature. Such information shall be maintained and
updated annually. The information may be available in print form.

JUSTIFICATION:
Veterans in New York State have been and continue to be vital to the
small business enterprises in the State. New York State has done too
little to assist veterans in playing a greater role in the economy by
forming and expanding small business enterprises. Medical advances and
new medical technologies have made it possible for service-disabled
veterans to play a greater role in the formation and expansion of small
business enterprises in New York State. New York State must provide
additional assistance and support to veterans to better inform them on
how to become an owner of small business and how to expand thereby
enabling them to realize the American dream that they fought and
protect. This bill is one step in the process.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2009: S.4431 - Referred to Veterans, Homeland Security & Military
Affairs A.7093 - Passed Assembly.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Minimal cost to the Division of Veterans' Affairs.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law, provided that any rules and regulations necessary for the
implementation of this act on its effective date shall be promulgated on
or before such date.
